```dafny
method sort_array(array: seq<int>) returns (result: seq<int>)
    requires array != null // Precondition: The input array must not be null
    ensures |result| == |array| // Postcondition: The output array has the same length as the input array
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |result| ==> result[i] in array // Postcondition: All elements in the result are from the input array
    ensures (array.Length == 0 ==> result == []) // Postcondition: If the input array is empty, the result is also empty
    ensures (array.Length == 1 ==> result == array) // Postcondition: If the input array has one element, the result is the same as the input
    ensures (sum(array[0], array[array.Length - 1]) % 2 == 0 ==> is_sorted(result, true)) // Postcondition: If the sum of the first and last element is even, the result is sorted in descending order
    ensures (sum(array[0], array[array.Length - 1]) % 2 == 1 ==> is_sorted(result, false)) // Postcondition: If the sum of the first and last element is odd, the result is sorted in ascending order

method is_sorted(arr: seq<int>, descending: bool) returns (b: bool)
    requires arr != null
    ensures b == (forall i, j :: 0 <= i < j < |arr| ==> (if descending then arr[i] >= arr[j] else arr[i] <= arr[j]))
```

def sort_array(array):
    """
    Given an array of non-negative integers, return a copy of the given array after sorting,
    you will sort the given array in ascending order if the sum( first index value, last index value) is odd,
    or sort it in descending order if the sum( first index value, last index value) is even.

    Note:
    * don't change the given array.

    Examples:
    * sort_array([]) => []
    * sort_array([5]) => [5]
    * sort_array([2, 4, 3, 0, 1, 5]) => [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    * sort_array([2, 4, 3, 0, 1, 5, 6]) => [6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
    """
problem_data.canonical_solution: return [] if len(array) == 0 else sorted(array, reverse= (array[0]+array[-1]) % 2 == 0)
